scope: Isolierter Browser mit simulierten Serverantworten. Kein Zugriff auf laufende BTS-/BTP-Turniere.
checks: Reset starts with a styled scope-and-area selector and no implicit deletion
Review shows the exact local reset areas and warns that a later sync can restore BTP values
Combining areas sends one explicit local maintenance plan and blocks duplicate actions
BTS and BTP supports field and pause resets but clearly excludes a full BTP wipe
Result selection excludes the running game and waits for a specific eligible match
The reset selector and its fixed actions fit at 1920 × 1000
The reset selector and its fixed actions fit at 950 × 1000
The reset selector and its fixed actions fit at 390 × 844
The reset selector and its fixed actions fit at 320 × 568
The reset selector and its fixed actions fit at 568 × 320
A lost BTP connection blocks review without losing selected matches
The final result confirmation identifies the selected game and its possible follow-up effect
A selected winner reset addresses only the reviewed game and includes BTP explicitly
A failed BTP verification is shown without claiming that the result reset succeeded
Every-game player check-in reset is available locally even while BTP is offline
The check-in confirmation names all games and preserves official attendance
Cancelling the check-in reset does not send a maintenance action
Confirming player check-ins sends exactly the selected bulk action without a match-result filter
Reset notifications update every game and retain the settings draft and success feedback
Full local reset is mutually exclusive with partial areas
Selecting a partial area removes the full-wipe selection
Changing to BTP removes an unsupported full-wipe selection instead of silently changing its scope
Escape dismisses selection without sending an operation
Field removal remains available when all games have one or two unknown opponents and no results
Unresolved opponents do not introduce a result or participant filter into the field reset command
Changing area disposes the selector without interrupting shared services
The self-check-in starts with both players present
Bulk reset immediately updates self-check-in cards while keeping the umpire present
